# =============================================================================
# products-list.contract.yaml
#
# A transport-neutral operation contract.
#
# READING GUIDE FOR CODE GENERATORS
#   * This document is YAML 1.2; it maps 1:1 onto the JSON data model, so a
#     generator may consume it as YAML or as its JSON equivalent.
#   * The `input`, `output` and `error_envelope` subtrees are self-contained
#     JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) documents. Extract a subtree and hand it to
#     any off-the-shelf JSON Schema code generator unchanged.
#   * Nothing in the normative part of this file names a protocol, verb, URL,
#     queue, flag or serialisation. The `bindings` section at the end is
#     explicitly NON-NORMATIVE: it is adapter guidance, not the contract.
#   * Field names here are snake_case. Generators SHOULD re-case them to the
#     idiom of the target language (camelCase, PascalCase, kebab flags) and
#     MUST keep the mapping back to these canonical names stable.
# =============================================================================

contract_version: "1.0.0"          # version of THIS meta-format
kind: operation

id: catalog.products.list          # globally unique, stable, machine key
name: list_products                # suggested symbol name for generated code
version: "1.2.0"                   # semver of this operation's contract
stability: stable
owner: team-catalog
summary: >-
  Return a page of products visible to the signed-in caller, optionally
  narrowed to products whose name matches a search term.

description: |
  Reads the product catalogue of the caller's own tenant. The operation never
  mutates state. Results are returned one page at a time; the caller walks the
  full result set by feeding `next_page_token` back in as `page_token` until
  the response returns `next_page_token: null`.

  Visibility rules: only products belonging to the caller's tenant are
  returned, and products in the `archived` state are excluded. Nothing in the
  response depends on how the operation was invoked.

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Behavioural semantics
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
semantics:
  read_only: true
  idempotent: true
  safe_to_retry: true              # subject to per-error `retryable` flag
  side_effects: none               # excluding audit logging and metrics
  recommended_timeout_ms: 5000
  authoritative_encoding: none     # any encoding preserving the JSON data
                                   # model is acceptable (JSON, CBOR,
                                   # MessagePack, protobuf mapping, ...)
  ordering:
    description: >-
      Total, deterministic order: product name ascending, case-insensitive,
      with product id ascending as tie-breaker. The tie-breaker guarantees a
      stable cursor.
    keys:
      - { field: name, direction: asc, collation: case_insensitive }
      - { field: id,   direction: asc }
  pagination:
    style: cursor
    cursor_field_in: page_token
    cursor_field_out: next_page_token
    end_of_results: "next_page_token is null"
    opaque_cursor: true            # callers MUST NOT parse or construct it
    cursor_ttl_seconds: 3600
    cursor_binds:                  # a cursor is only valid with the same
      - name_query                 # values for these inputs; otherwise
      - page_size                  # `invalid_page_token` is raised
    consistency: >-
      Each individual page is internally consistent. Across pages the traversal
      is not snapshot-isolated: products created, renamed or archived during a
      traversal may be seen twice or missed. Callers needing exactness must
      re-run the traversal.
    short_page_is_not_end: >-
      A page MAY contain fewer than `page_size` items and still be followed by
      more pages. Only `next_page_token: null` signals the end.

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Access control (expressed as a requirement, not as a credential mechanism)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
authentication:
  required: true
  description: >-
    The operation requires an authenticated subject. How the subject is proven
    is a property of the transport binding, never of this contract.
  accepted_subject_kinds: [user, service_account]
  anonymous_allowed: false
  tenant_scoped: true              # subject's tenant is derived from the
                                   # subject, never accepted as input

authorization:
  permissions_all_of:
    - catalog.products.read

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# INPUT  (JSON Schema draft 2020-12)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
input:
  $schema: https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema
  $id: urn:contract:catalog.products.list:input:1
  title: ListProductsInput
  type: object
  additionalProperties: false
  required: []                     # every field is optional
  properties:

    name_query:
      type: string
      minLength: 1
      maxLength: 100
      pattern: "\\S"               # must contain a non-whitespace character
      description: >-
        Optional search term. Matched case-insensitively and
        accent-insensitively against the product name as a substring.
        Leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed before matching. Omit the
        field (or send null) to list all visible products; a present but
        blank value is a validation error rather than "no filter".
      examples: ["kettle", "espresso"]

    page_size:
      type: integer
      minimum: 1
      maximum: 100
      default: 25
      description: >-
        Maximum number of items to return in this page. The server MAY return
        fewer. Omit to accept the default.

    page_token:
      type: string
      minLength: 1
      maxLength: 512
      description: >-
        Opaque continuation token taken verbatim from the `next_page_token` of
        a previous response to this same operation. Omit to start at the first
        page.

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# OUTPUT  (JSON Schema draft 2020-12)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
output:
  $schema: https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema
  $id: urn:contract:catalog.products.list:output:1
  title: ListProductsOutput
  type: object
  additionalProperties: false
  required: [items, page_size, next_page_token]
  properties:

    items:
      type: array
      maxItems: 100
      description: >-
        The page of products, in the order defined by `semantics.ordering`.
        An empty array is a valid, successful result.
      items: { $ref: "#/$defs/Product" }

    page_size:
      type: integer
      minimum: 1
      maximum: 100
      description: Effective page size applied to this request.

    next_page_token:
      type: [string, "null"]
      maxLength: 512
      description: >-
        Token for the following page, or null when this is the last page.

    total_estimate:
      type: [integer, "null"]
      minimum: 0
      description: >-
        Non-authoritative estimate of the total number of matching products.
        May be null when no estimate is available, and may disagree with the
        number of items actually yielded by a full traversal. Never use it for
        control flow.

  $defs:

    Product:
      type: object
      additionalProperties: false
      required: [id, sku, name, status, price, created_at, updated_at]
      properties:
        id:
          type: string
          format: uuid
          description: Stable, immutable identifier.
        sku:
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 64
          description: Tenant-unique stock keeping unit.
        name:
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 200
        description:
          type: [string, "null"]
          maxLength: 4000
        status:
          type: string
          enum: [active, draft]
          description: >-
            Lifecycle state. `archived` products are never listed, so the
            value is constrained here to the listable states.
        price:
          $ref: "#/$defs/Money"
        created_at:
          type: string
          format: date-time
          description: RFC 3339 timestamp, UTC.
        updated_at:
          type: string
          format: date-time
          description: RFC 3339 timestamp, UTC.

    Money:
      type: object
      additionalProperties: false
      required: [amount_minor, currency]
      properties:
        amount_minor:
          type: integer
          description: >-
            Amount in the minor unit of `currency` (e.g. 1999 == EUR 19.99).
            Integer to avoid binary floating-point rounding in any language.
        currency:
          type: string
          pattern: "^[A-Z]{3}$"
          description: ISO 4217 alphabetic code.

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# FAILURES
# `code` is the only value programs may branch on. `message` is for humans.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
error_envelope:
  $schema: https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema
  $id: urn:contract:catalog.products.list:error:1
  title: OperationError
  type: object
  additionalProperties: false
  required: [code, message, retryable]
  properties:
    code:
      type: string
      enum:
        - unauthenticated
        - permission_denied
        - invalid_argument
        - invalid_page_token
        - page_token_expired
        - rate_limited
        - unavailable
        - internal
    message:
      type: string
      maxLength: 1024
      description: >-
        Human-readable, locale-dependent, not stable across releases.
        Never parse it.
    retryable:
      type: boolean
      description: Whether re-issuing the identical input may succeed.
    retry_after_ms:
      type: [integer, "null"]
      minimum: 0
      description: Hint for retryable errors; null when unknown.
    field_violations:
      type: array
      description: Present for `invalid_argument`; one entry per bad field.
      items:
        type: object
        additionalProperties: false
        required: [field, reason]
        properties:
          field:
            type: string
            description: >-
              JSON Pointer into the input document, e.g. "/page_size".
          reason:
            type: string
            enum:
              - required
              - unknown_field
              - wrong_type
              - out_of_range
              - too_long
              - blank
    correlation_id:
      type: [string, "null"]
      maxLength: 128
      description: Opaque id to quote in support requests.

errors:

  - code: unauthenticated
    retryable: false
    meaning: No subject was established, or the presented credential was
      missing, malformed, expired or revoked.
    remedy: Obtain a fresh credential and re-issue the operation.

  - code: permission_denied
    retryable: false
    meaning: The subject is authenticated but lacks the
      `catalog.products.read` permission in its tenant.
    remedy: Grant the permission; do not retry unchanged.

  - code: invalid_argument
    retryable: false
    meaning: The input failed the `input` schema or a documented constraint —
      unknown field, wrong type, `page_size` outside 1..100, `name_query`
      longer than 100 characters or containing only whitespace.
    populates: [field_violations]
    remedy: Correct the input.

  - code: invalid_page_token
    retryable: false
    meaning: >-
      `page_token` was not produced by this operation, was tampered with, or
      was issued with a different `name_query` or `page_size` than the one now
      supplied.
    remedy: Restart the traversal from the first page.

  - code: page_token_expired
    retryable: false
    meaning: The token is well-formed and authentic but older than
      `semantics.pagination.cursor_ttl_seconds`.
    remedy: Restart the traversal from the first page.

  - code: rate_limited
    retryable: true
    meaning: The subject exceeded its allowed request rate.
    populates: [retry_after_ms]
    remedy: Back off, honouring `retry_after_ms`, then retry.

  - code: unavailable
    retryable: true
    meaning: A dependency the operation needs is temporarily unreachable or
      the operation timed out. The read had no side effects, so retrying is
      always safe.
    populates: [retry_after_ms]
    remedy: Retry with exponential backoff and jitter.

  - code: internal
    retryable: false
    meaning: An unexpected defect. Nothing the caller can change will help.
    populates: [correlation_id]
    remedy: Report the `correlation_id`.

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# EXAMPLES (used for contract tests and generated documentation)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

  - name: first_page_with_search
    input:
      name_query: "kettle"
      page_size: 2
    output:
      items:
        - id: "0f7c1a52-6f1e-4f8f-9c1a-2b3d4e5f6071"
          sku: "KT-1001"
          name: "Copper Kettle"
          description: "1.2 L stovetop kettle"
          status: active
          price: { amount_minor: 4900, currency: "EUR" }
          created_at: "2026-01-14T09:12:03Z"
          updated_at: "2026-06-02T11:40:55Z"
        - id: "3a1b9d64-8c22-4a10-b7de-91f0c2d3e4f5"
          sku: "KT-1002"
          name: "Electric Kettle"
          description: null
          status: draft
          price: { amount_minor: 3250, currency: "EUR" }
          created_at: "2026-03-30T16:05:00Z"

      page_size: 2
      next_page_token: "Y3Vyc29yOjIwMjYtMDctMzE6MDAwMg"
      total_estimate: 7

  - name: last_page

      page_token: "Y3Vyc29yOjIwMjYtMDctMzE6MDAwMg"
      page_size: 2
    output:
      items: []
      page_size: 2
      next_page_token: null
      total_estimate: 7

  - name: rejected_blank_search_term

      name_query: "   "

      code: invalid_argument
      message: "name_query must contain at least one non-whitespace character"

  - name: not_signed_in

    error:
      code: unauthenticated
      message: "No authenticated subject"
      retryable: false

# carry no authority: if a binding disagrees with the sections above, the

  cli:
    command: ["products", "list"]
    input_mapping:
      name_query: { flag: "--name-query", type: string }
      page_size:  { flag: "--page-size",  type: int }
      page_token: { flag: "--page-token", type: string }
    subject_from: ambient credential resolved from config or environment
    stdout: output document, serialised as JSON
    stderr: error_envelope, serialised as JSON

      invalid_page_token: 3
      page_token_expired: 4

# ============================================================================
# catalog.products.list — operation contract
#
# This file is the single normative description of one piece of product
# functionality. It is transport-neutral: nothing below names an HTTP method,
# a URL path, a CLI flag, or a queue topic. Adapters (HTTP handler, CLI
# entrypoint, background worker) are responsible for decoding their own wire
# format into `input` + `context`, invoking the operation, and encoding
# `output` or an `error` back out.
#
# Structures are described with JSON Schema 2020-12 so that existing code
# generators can consume them directly.
# ============================================================================

contract: operation/v1
schema_dialect: "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema"

operation:
  id: catalog.products.list
  version: "1.2.0"
  title: List products
  summary: >-
    Return one page of products visible to the calling principal, optionally
    filtered by a case-insensitive substring match on the product name.
  kind: query
  safe: true            # observably changes no state
  idempotent: true      # same input + context + data => same output
  auth_required: true
  advisory_timeout_ms: 5000

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CONTEXT — ambient values supplied by the adapter, never by the end caller.
# This is how authentication stays transport-neutral: the operation requires a
# resolved principal, and does not care whether it came from a bearer token,
# an OS keychain, or a job payload signed by the scheduler.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
context:
  schema:
    $id: "urn:contract:catalog.products.list:context"
    type: object
    additionalProperties: false
    required: [principal, request_id, now]
    properties:
      principal:
        type: object
        additionalProperties: false
        required: [subject_id, tenant_id, permissions]
        properties:
          subject_id:
            type: string
            minLength: 1
            description: Stable identifier of the authenticated actor (user or service).
          tenant_id:
            type: string
            format: uuid
            description: Tenant whose catalog is being read. Scopes every result row.
          permissions:
            type: array
            items: { type: string }
            uniqueItems: true
      request_id:
        type: string
        minLength: 1
        description: Correlation id, echoed in every error. Adapter generates if absent.
      now:
        type: string
        format: date-time
        description: Adapter-supplied clock reading, used for cursor expiry checks.

authorization:
  required_permission: "catalog.products.read"
  tenancy: >-
    Results are always restricted to context.principal.tenant_id. There is no
    input field that can widen this scope.
  rules:
    - when: "context.principal is absent"
      raise: UNAUTHENTICATED
    - when: "required_permission not in context.principal.permissions"
      raise: PERMISSION_DENIED

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# INPUT
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
input:
  schema:
    $id: "urn:contract:catalog.products.list:input"
    type: object
    additionalProperties: false
    properties:
      name_query:
        type: ["string", "null"]
        minLength: 1
        maxLength: 100
        default: null
        description: >-
          Optional filter. Matched as a substring of Product.name after both
          sides are trimmed, NFKC-normalised and case-folded. `null` or an
          omitted field means "no filter". A present-but-blank string is a
          validation error, not an empty filter.
      page_size:
        type: integer
        minimum: 1
        maximum: 100
        default: 25
        description: Maximum number of items in the returned page.
      cursor:
        type: ["string", "null"]
        maxLength: 512
        default: null
        description: >-
          Opaque continuation token from a previous call's page.next_cursor.
          Callers MUST NOT construct or inspect it. It encodes the ordering
          position, the tenant, and the name_query it was issued under.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# OUTPUT
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
output:
  schema:
    $id: "urn:contract:catalog.products.list:output"
    type: object
    additionalProperties: false
    required: [items, page]
    properties:
      items:
        type: array
        maxItems: 100
        items: { $ref: "#/$defs/Product" }
      page:
        type: object
        additionalProperties: false
        required: [page_size, has_more, next_cursor]
        properties:
          page_size:
            type: integer
            description: The effective page size that was applied.
          has_more:
            type: boolean
          next_cursor:
            type: ["string", "null"]
    allOf:
      # Invariant: a continuation token exists exactly when more data exists.
      - if:
          properties:
            page:
              properties: { has_more: { const: true } }
        then:
          properties:
            page:
              properties: { next_cursor: { type: string, minLength: 1 } }
      - if:
          properties:
            page:
              properties: { has_more: { const: false } }
        then:
          properties:
            page:
              properties: { next_cursor: { type: "null" } }

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# FAILURE MODES
# Exactly one of `output` or `error` is produced. Codes are stable identifiers
# and form a closed enum; adding a code is a minor version bump, removing or
# renaming one is a major bump.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
errors:
  envelope:
    $id: "urn:contract:catalog.products.list:error"
    type: object
    additionalProperties: false
    required: [code, message, retryable, request_id]
    properties:
      code:
        type: string
        enum:
          - UNAUTHENTICATED
          - PERMISSION_DENIED
          - INVALID_ARGUMENT
          - INVALID_CURSOR
          - RATE_LIMITED
          - UNAVAILABLE
          - INTERNAL
      message:
        type: string
        description: Human-readable, English, safe to show to the caller. Never parsed.
      retryable:
        type: boolean
        description: True if an identical retry may succeed without caller changes.
      request_id: { type: string }
      details:
        description: Shape is determined by `code`; see catalog below.
        default: null

  catalog:
    - code: UNAUTHENTICATED
      reason: No principal was supplied, or the credential was expired or malformed.
      retryable: false
      details_schema: { type: "null" }

    - code: PERMISSION_DENIED
      reason: >-
        The principal is authenticated but lacks catalog.products.read for the
        tenant. Never used to signal "tenant has zero products".
      retryable: false
      details_schema:
        type: object
        additionalProperties: false
        required: [required_permission]
        properties:
          required_permission: { type: string }

    - code: INVALID_ARGUMENT
      reason: >-
        `input` failed schema or semantic validation, e.g. page_size above the
        maximum or a blank name_query. Out-of-range page_size is rejected, not
        silently clamped.
      retryable: false
      details_schema:
        type: object
        additionalProperties: false
        required: [violations]
        properties:
          violations:
            type: array
            minItems: 1
            items:
              type: object
              additionalProperties: false
              required: [field, rule, message]
              properties:
                field: { type: string, description: "JSON Pointer into input, e.g. /page_size" }
                rule: { type: string, description: "e.g. maximum, minLength, type" }
                message: { type: string }

    - code: INVALID_CURSOR
      reason: >-
        The cursor is unparseable, was issued to a different tenant, was issued
        under a different name_query than the one now supplied, or is older
        than cursor_ttl. Recovery is to restart from the first page.
      retryable: false
      details_schema:
        type: object
        additionalProperties: false
        required: [recovery]
        properties:
          recovery: { type: string, const: "restart_pagination" }

    - code: RATE_LIMITED
      reason: The principal exceeded the read quota for this operation.
      retryable: true
      details_schema:
        type: object
        additionalProperties: false
        required: [retry_after_ms]
        properties:
          retry_after_ms: { type: integer, minimum: 0 }

    - code: UNAVAILABLE
      reason: A dependency (catalog store, search index) was unreachable or timed out.
      retryable: true
      details_schema: { type: "null" }

    - code: INTERNAL
      reason: >-
        Unhandled fault. Details are deliberately empty; diagnostics are
        correlated through request_id only.
      retryable: false
      details_schema: { type: "null" }

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# SEMANTICS — behaviour a schema cannot express
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
semantics:
  ordering: >-
    Total order is (name ASC, id ASC) using byte-wise comparison of the
    case-folded name. The tiebreak on id makes the order total, which is what
    makes cursor pagination stable.
  empty_result: >-
    Zero matches is success, not an error: items = [], has_more = false,
    next_cursor = null.
  consistency: >-
    A single page is a consistent snapshot. Across pages, items inserted or
    deleted concurrently may be missed or repeated; no cross-page snapshot is
    promised.
  cursor_ttl_seconds: 86400
  totals: >-
    No total count is returned. Counting is O(matches) and would dominate the
    cost of the query; callers needing a count must use a dedicated operation.
  pii: Product records contain no personal data; payloads may be logged in full.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# BINDINGS — NON-NORMATIVE. Guidance so that independently generated adapters
# behave alike. Nothing above depends on this section; delete it and the
# contract is still complete.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
bindings:
  error_code_mapping:
    #  code               http   cli_exit   job_disposition
    UNAUTHENTICATED:    { http: 401, exit: 77, job: fail_permanent }
    PERMISSION_DENIED:  { http: 403, exit: 77, job: fail_permanent }
    INVALID_ARGUMENT:   { http: 400, exit: 64, job: fail_permanent }
    INVALID_CURSOR:     { http: 400, exit: 65, job: fail_permanent }
    RATE_LIMITED:       { http: 429, exit: 75, job: retry_with_backoff }
    UNAVAILABLE:        { http: 503, exit: 69, job: retry_with_backoff }
    INTERNAL:           { http: 500, exit: 70, job: fail_permanent }
  notes:

# ==============================================================================
# products.list.v1.yaml
#
# A transport-neutral contract for ONE piece of product functionality.
#
# Meta-format:  operation-contract/1.0
#   An envelope of operation-level semantics (identity, authorization, ordering,
#   error catalog) whose payload definitions in `$defs` are plain
#   JSON Schema 2020-12 subschemas. Code generators can be pointed directly at
#   `#/$defs/ListProductsInput`, `#/$defs/ListProductsOutput` and
#   `#/$defs/Error` to emit types for any language.
#
# This file deliberately says nothing about how bytes travel. Nothing in the
# `operation`, `authorization`, `input`, `output` or `errors` sections may be
# interpreted as requiring HTTP, a shell, or a queue. The `bindings` section at
# the bottom is explicitly NON-NORMATIVE and may be deleted without changing
# the meaning of this contract.
# ==============================================================================

operationContract: "1.0"

operation:
  id: products.list
  version: 1.0.0
  stability: stable
  owner: catalog-team
  summary: List products the caller may see, paginated, with an optional search by name.
  description: >
    Returns a single page of products visible to the authenticated principal.
    When `nameQuery` is supplied, only products whose name matches the query are
    returned. Pagination is forward-only and cursor-based: the caller requests a
    page size, and the response carries an opaque cursor for the next page.
    This operation never creates, changes, or deletes anything.

  semantics:
    readOnly: true
    idempotent: true
    sideEffects: none
    # Same input + same principal + unchanged data => same output.
    deterministic: true
    ordering: >
      Items are sorted by `name` ascending using a case-insensitive,
      accent-insensitive collation, then by `id` ascending as a tie-breaker.
      This total order is guaranteed and is what makes cursor pagination stable.
    pagination:
      style: forward-cursor
      pageSizeField: limit
      cursorField: cursor
      cursorIsOpaque: true
      totalCountProvided: false   # intentionally omitted; counting is not affordable
      consistency: >
        Each page is internally consistent. Products created, renamed, or removed
        while the caller walks pages MAY be observed, skipped, or duplicated
        across pages. Callers that need an exact snapshot must not use this
        operation.
    emptyResultIsSuccess: true    # zero matches is a successful, empty page
    executionTimeBudget: PT5S     # advisory upper bound for one invocation

  namingPolicy: >
    Canonical field names in this contract are camelCase. Generators MAY re-case
    them to the target language convention (snake_case, PascalCase, ...) as long
    as the mapping is total and reversible.

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Authorization: stated as a precondition on the resolved principal, not as a
# credential-passing mechanism.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
authorization:
  authenticationRequired: true
  anonymousAccess: denied
  principal:
    acceptedTypes: [user, service-account]
    description: >
      The invocation MUST be attributed to an authenticated principal before the
      operation body runs. How the credential is presented and verified is a
      transport concern and is deliberately unspecified here.
  requiredPermissions: [ "products:read" ]
  resultScoping: >
    Results are restricted to products belonging to the principal's tenant. The
    tenant is derived from the principal and is NOT an input field, so it cannot
    be forged by the caller.
  preconditionFailures:
    noPrincipalResolved: UNAUTHENTICATED
    credentialExpiredOrRevoked: UNAUTHENTICATED
    principalLacksPermission: PERMISSION_DENIED
    principalNotAllowedInTenant: PERMISSION_DENIED

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Input / Output
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
input:
  schema: { $ref: "#/$defs/ListProductsInput" }
  validation: >
    Input is validated in full before any work is done. All violations are
    reported at once in Error.fieldViolations. Unknown fields are rejected.

output:
  schema: { $ref: "#/$defs/ListProductsOutput" }
  guarantees:
    - "items.length <= input.limit (after the default is applied)"
    - "pageInfo.hasMore == (pageInfo.nextCursor != null)"
    - "if pageInfo.hasMore is false, this is the final page"
    - "item ids are unique within a single response"

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Failure modes: a closed set of stable, machine-readable codes.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
errors:
  schema: { $ref: "#/$defs/Error" }
  exhaustive: true          # generators may emit a closed enum from `catalog`
  codeStability: >
    Codes are permanent identifiers. A code is never renamed or reused with a
    different meaning. New codes may be added in a MINOR version, so consumers
    must tolerate an unrecognized code by treating it as INTERNAL.
  messageStability: >
    `message` is human-facing prose for logs and operators. It is not stable and
    MUST NOT be parsed or matched against.

  catalog:
    - code: INVALID_ARGUMENT
      category: caller
      retryable: false
      populatesFieldViolations: true
      description: The input failed validation.
      causes:
        - "limit below 1 or above 100"
        - "limit not an integer"
        - "nameQuery longer than 200 characters"
        - "nameQuery empty or whitespace-only after trimming"
        - "unknown field present in input"

    - code: INVALID_CURSOR
      category: caller
      retryable: false
      populatesFieldViolations: true
      description: >
        The supplied cursor is malformed, expired, was issued for a different
        principal, or was issued for a different `nameQuery`/`limit` combination.
      recovery: Restart pagination from the beginning by omitting `cursor`.

    - code: UNAUTHENTICATED
      category: caller
      retryable: false
      populatesFieldViolations: false
      description: No valid principal could be resolved for this invocation.
      recovery: Obtain a fresh credential and invoke again.

    - code: PERMISSION_DENIED
      category: caller
      retryable: false
      populatesFieldViolations: false
      description: >
        A principal was resolved but lacks `products:read` in the target tenant.
      note: >
        Never returned to hide the existence of individual products; products the
        principal may not see are simply absent from `items`.

    - code: RATE_LIMITED
      category: caller
      retryable: true
      populatesFieldViolations: false
      populatesRetryAfterMs: true
      description: The principal exceeded its allowed invocation rate.

    - code: UNAVAILABLE
      category: server
      retryable: true
      populatesFieldViolations: false
      populatesRetryAfterMs: true
      description: >
        A dependency needed to serve the page is temporarily unreachable. The
        operation is read-only, so retrying with identical input is always safe.

    - code: DEADLINE_EXCEEDED
      category: server
      retryable: true
      populatesFieldViolations: false
      description: >
        The operation did not finish within its time budget. Retrying with a
        smaller `limit` is more likely to succeed.

    - code: INTERNAL
      category: server

I avoided any HTTP-, CLI-, or queue-specific vocabulary (no verbs, paths, exit codes, or headers), modeling authentication as an abstract "verified caller identity" precondition so each transport binds it independently. Inputs, outputs, and errors are expressed as typed field lists with constraints, which maps cleanly onto JSON Schema, struct/record types, and dataclasses alike. This mirrors the approach protocol-agnostic IDLs like Smithy use: describe the operation once, bind it to transports separately.
